title: Vendor onramp mini-canvas and acceptance matrix
content:
Purpose
This note is a compact working canvas to get a partner from initial ingestion -> publishable tile in a single sprint. Focused on minimal acceptance criteria (technical + copy) so engineering and GTM agree on a fast path while capturing risks for enterprise partners.

Quick summary / goals
- Reduce partner onramp cycle from 6+ weeks to 1–2 sprints for straightforward integrations.
- Produce 3 publish-ready copy variants (hero + 30 char tile + 1-sentence summary) and one compliance signoff artifact per partner.
- Capture gating matrix so we can automate acceptance checks in the onboarding tracker (JIRA / spreadsheet).

Canvas sections (mini)
1) Partner metadata snapshot (minimal fields we need to publish)
   - Partner name (normalized): e.g., Acme VectorOps
   - Short category: embeddings / reranking / hosted connector
   - Supported integrations: SSO, KMS, VPC? (Y/N)
   - Primary contact + legal ready? (Contact + signoff state)

2) Must-have technical gates (binary checks, owner)
   - Endpoint contract conformance: compatible with Redwood API shapes (owner: eng-interop) -> PASS/FAIL
   - Auth model: OAuth2/SAML/Token mapping validated (owner: security) -> PASS/FAIL
   - Data residency: if requested, region coverage confirmed (owner: infra) -> PASS/FAIL
   - Metrics/telemetry: partner supplies usage events or we can proxy (owner: observability) -> PASS/FAIL
   - Billing mapping: SKU decisions & pricing input (owner: finance) -> PASS/FAIL
   - Certs & TLS: certificate chain validated (owner: infra) -> PASS/FAIL

3) Copy & UX deliverables (GTM)
   - Hero line (3 variants) -> select 1
   - 30-char tile text (A/B variants) -> select 1
   - 1-sentence product summary (for marketplace tile detail)
   - 3 bullet feature list (for expanded tile)
   - Short demo flow / try-it instructions (for sandbox)

Acceptance matrix (simple risk ratings)
- Low friction: no private network needs, uses Redwood-hosted model, no enterprise legal. (Fast path)
- Medium friction: SSO + KMS required, minor infra changes, legal review pending. (1–2 sprints)
- High friction: On-prem bundle, SOC2/ISO artifacts not present, complex billing. (Escalate to enterprise onboarding)

Sample copy experiments (working drafts)
Hero variants (tone: product-focused / trust / developer-first)
   1. "Ship vector search that scales — plug Acme into Redwood in minutes."
   2. "High-throughput embeddings, lower inference cost. Launch with Acme."
   3. "Developer-first semantic search powered by Acme + Redwood."

30-char tile variants\   
   - "Embeddings: Acme + Redwood"
   - "Fast semantic search"
   - "Scale embeddings, cut cost"

One-line summary examples\   
   - "Acme VectorOps provides production-grade embeddings that integrate with Redwood’s runtime for low-latency semantic search."
   - "Combine Acme’s vector store with Redwood’s inference routing to deliver reliable semantic search at scale."

Feature bullets (for expanded tile)
   - "Low-latency embeddings optimized for long-context retrieval"
   - "Transparent pricing & commit options for high-volume workloads"
   - "Enterprise-ready: SSO, KMS, and audit logs supported"

Technical gating checklist (detailed)
- API schema compatibility: example request/response included in partner artifact (Y/N). If N, provide mapping tasks.
- Auth flows tested: sample access token exchange recorded in test log (link).
- End-to-end smoke: produce a demo request -> generate token -> call -> validate response (owner + link to smoke test).
- Error modes documented: expected 4xx/5xx and retry guidance.

Non-functional requirements (NFRs)
- Latency targets: average p50 < 150ms for tile demo path (if low-latency product) / accept higher for batch jobs
- Rate limits: agreed burst and steady state (e.g., 100 rps burst, 10 rps steady)
- Observability: partner events mapped to our tracing (X-Request-Id)

Compliance & legal quick hits
- Data processing addendum: partner must accept DPA template OR provide equivalent language
- Sensitive vertical flags: health / finance customers need documented controls (flagged in matrix)
- Export controls: partner declares geos for data transfer

Localization / metadata suggestions
- Suggested categories: "Embeddings", "Search & Retrieval", "Data Connectors"
- Suggested keywords (tags): embeddings, semantic-search, vector-store, k8s, sso

Launch logistics (minimal sprint plan)
- Week 0: Contract + partner intake form
- Week 1: Technical integration + smoke test (eng-interop)
- Week 2: Copy freeze, legal checklist, pricing SKU mapping
- Week 3: Marketplace publish + monitor first 24h metrics

Open questions / operating assumptions (notes to self)
- If partner requires on-prem agent to run in their VPC, this becomes a high-friction flow and needs solutions-eng involvement (ticket: SOL-214).
- Who signs off final pricing? Assume partner and finance lead (Priya) need to approve; capture as gating item.
- Do we need a templated sandbox for partners to try the tile? If yes, build minimal demo container image.

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: copy claims that imply SLAs ("<50ms"). Mitigation: avoid numeric latency claims — use qualitative language or tie to commit tiers.
- Risk: missing DPA prolongs legal review. Mitigation: require executed DPA before publish; offer partner DPA checklist.

Next steps (owner + ETA)
- Maya: draft final hero + tile variants and place in shared creative folder (ETA: +3 business days)
- Liam: add acceptance matrix checks to JIRA GTM-881 and create checklist subtasks (ETA: +2 business days)
- Priya: confirm SKU mapping with finance (ETA: +5 business days)
- Dmitry: smoke test template and quick-run script (ETA: +4 business days)

Appendix: quick content examples for copy team to iterate on
- Micro-CTA examples: "Try in sandbox", "Request a commit", "Get started — 5 min setup"
- Support blurb for tile: "Includes docs, quickstart and one production-grade integration guide."

Unresolved items to bring to sprint planning
- Need decision on whether we allow partner-supplied demo data on sandbox (privacy concern).
- Agree on acceptable latency wording for public tile.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally concise; treat it as a checklist-first working doc. Pull copy variants into the creative board and do 1 small copy A/B on tile text before publish.
- If partner is enterprise-tier, clone this doc and move to product/private-deployments handoff flow.

End of canvas

-- Maya
